A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same vCache research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support comparison, including matching material across relocations and renumbering.

before.justification: v3 reports original cache-error, cache-hit, latency, and benchmark analyses in Section 5 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v4 retains original benchmark experiments and reports additional overhead, vLLM integration, and policy-ablation results in Appendix D.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–2 retain the same per-embedding logistic model, confidence-bound calculation, and randomized exploration policy. The architecture overview explains this existing procedure; the added policy variants are comparison methods.

E1.justification: Both versions use SemCacheClassification, SemCacheLMArena, and SemCacheSearchQueries, with the same underlying datasets and benchmark construction. The added vLLM and ablation experiments reuse this coverage.

E2.justification: Beyond the retained static-threshold and fine-tuned-embedding comparisons, v4 Table 3 evaluates global dynamic thresholds (GD), local logistic thresholds (LD1), and local sigmoid probabilities (LD2). Table 2 adds a vLLM-only comparator. LS has no reported results; GS and LD3 correspond to GPTCache and vCache.

E3.justification: v4 adds evaluation with Llama 3.1 70B served through vLLM on two GPUs, using 45,000 classification prompts and error tolerances of 0.01–0.03, alongside the new policy comparisons. The search-query tracking plot changes its stated tolerance from 0.015 to 0.02, and the Pareto threshold sweep changes. These do not establish reruns under identical settings.

E4.justification: v4 Appendix D.5 adds component ablations examining global versus per-embedding thresholds and threshold-only, sigmoid, and confidence-bound policies. Appendices D.3–D.4 additionally examine logistic-fitting overhead and benefits alongside optimized inference. v3 lacks these component and deployment analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions specify 95% confidence intervals using Wallis binomial bounds and contingency tests, and retain the embedding-latency percentile whisker plots. v4 introduces no new seed information, repeated-run counts, or statistical estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Main Figures 4–5 are retained, but the search-query results change: v3 Figures 6–7 report vCache underperforming static baselines, whereas v4 Figures 7–8 report an advantage under revised sweeps. New results include 0.0017-second logistic fitting, Table 2 runtimes of 240 minutes without caching versus 214, 170, and 160 minutes with caching, and Table 3 policy comparisons.

T1.justification: Definition 4.1, Theorem 4.1, the substantive equations, and the proof moved from Appendix B to C remain unchanged, including the i.i.d. and sigmoid assumptions. The glossary and fixed-time clarification explain existing mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the central claims of verified caching with user-defined error bounds, online per-embedding learning, embedding independence, and three released benchmarks. The introductory claims of up to twice the cache-hit rate and sixfold lower error also remain.

C2.justification: v4 adds a single-turn, short-to-medium-context applicability description and explains the heterogeneous classification benchmark as testing generalization across domains. It interprets the new ablations as supporting probabilistic error control and the vLLM experiment as demonstrating complementary benefits. The principal judge-dependence and modeling-assumption limitations remain.

D1.justification: v4 discloses CPU fitting with sklearn.linear_model, the 70B vLLM deployment setup, and explicit benchmark-specific response-equivalence checks. Appendix F adds configuration guidance, suggesting error bounds such as 0.5% or 2–3% depending on application requirements. Code and benchmark access remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v4 adds LLM background references and citations to vLLM and SGLang, positioning semantic caching as complementary to inference optimization. Appendix D.5 explicitly describes vCache as adaptive, probabilistic, and Bayesian. Its central positioning against static thresholds and embedding fine-tuning remains.

P1.justification: v4 expands the introduction, condenses related work, and adds notation and workflow explanations. It reorganizes the appendices, removes the broader-impacts paragraph, and updates author information. The main section sequence and much of the methodological narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: v4 adds an architecture diagram, a notation table, and two experimental tables; relocates the introductory plots; and redraws the search-query displays. It also substantially restyles the title block, headings, running headers, and appendix layouts, while retaining most existing benchmark graphics.

improvement.justification: The added component ablations, measured fitting overhead, and vLLM comparison make the design choices and practical benefits better supported than in v3. The glossary and configuration guidance improve usability. These gains are limited by the insufficiently reconciled search-query result reversal and changed settings, which prevent treating the stronger performance report itself as established improvement.
